steps: On the Hobbing Machine, the broached component is hobbed to create an involute spur gear profile by performing a hobbing operation at a speed of 250 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, taking 1 minute to complete, after which the resulting hobbied gear is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On a Horizontal Milling Machine, a finish milling operation is performed on the Milled part for 32 minutes, using a milling speed of 1800 rpm and a climb milling tool path with contour following to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a Finished machined component that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

Perform surface grinding on a planed part using a grinding machine with an aluminum oxide, 60 grit grinding wheel rotating at 3500 sfm and a feed rate of 0.005 mm/pass for 15 minutes, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a ground part is subjected to wire EDM cutting in fine finish mode with automatic edge trimming and deionized water as the dielectric fluid, resulting in a precision finished milled part, and the process takes 15 minutes before the output is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to rough turning for 72 minutes using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a spindle speed of 600 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 10 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, resulting in a drilled component, and the operation takes 41 minutes before the output is placed on a conveyor belt.

The milled part is shaped on a shaper using a high-speed steel single-point tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute, taking 49 minutes to complete, after which the resulting shaped part is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, machining a 24-tooth spur gear at a shaping speed of 120 rpm, with the input component loaded from the MobileRobot and the finished part transferred to the ConveyorBelt, taking 17 minutes.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, a precision milling operation is performed on the milled part received from the ConveyorBelt, using a 6-axis synchronized tool head with an active damping system engaged to achieve a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to the MobileRobot after processing for 12 minutes.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on the honed cylinder, using a 220 mesh grit size to achieve a bore size of 50.00 ±0.01 mm, taking 39 minutes to complete, after which the precision finished part is transferred to the conveyor belt.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part using a pull-type internal broach with a depth of cut of 1.5 mm per tooth to achieve a Class 7 fit, taking 66 minutes, after which the broached component is transferred to a MobileRobot.

On the CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed on the lathed part, which is loaded from the MobileRobot, using CNC program #1045 with verified and loaded tool offsets and a spindle speed of 750 rpm, processing for 64 minutes to produce a finished machined component that is then transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

A face milling operation is performed on a vertical milling machine for 10 minutes, using a lathed part fed from a conveyor belt, with a carbide end mill of 16 mm diameter rotating at 1200 rpm and a depth of cut of 2.0 mm, resulting in a milled part loaded onto a mobile robot.

On the Bandsaw, a Metal bar is cut off into a Lathed part through a Cutting Off operation lasting 24 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade at a saw speed of 60 m/min and producing a 3.2 mm kerf, with the resulting Lathed part placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The milled part is planed on a Planer for 60 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 1.0 mm, a feed rate of 0.25 mm/stroke, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component, using a 25 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute with automatically calibrated die alignment, processing the material for 76 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

A drilled component is loaded from a conveyor belt onto a vertical lathe where a facing and turning operation is performed using a multi-pass facing and diameter reduction toolpath with a precision level of ±0.02 mm tolerance, resulting in a final drilled and shaped part, which is then transferred to a mobile robot, and the machining process runs for 72 minutes.

On a Screw Machines, a lathed part is subjected to screw threading to create an M12 metric coarse thread with a 1.75 mm pitch, running for 47 minutes at a production rate of 400 parts per hour, during which the input lathed parts are transferred from a MobileRobot to a ConveyorBelt as the resulting screwed components.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal fed from a conveyor belt, cutting it into sheared sheet metal pieces at a rate of 2 cuts per minute using a hardened tool steel blade with a 20 mm thickness and a shear angle of 1.5 degrees, with the finished parts being transferred to a mobile robot after processing for 99 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal for 92 minutes, using a 3000 W laser power and a cutting speed of 4.5 m/min with nitrogen gas assist at 20 bar, transforming the input material into cut sheet metal, which is then placed on a conveyor belt.

On the Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth through a gear shaping operation running at 120 strokes per minute for 28 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

Using a Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched for 62 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product with holes of 12 mm diameter, using an automatic centering die alignment and a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute, after which the cut sheet metal is transferred to a MobileRobot.

A vertical milling operation is performed on a lathed part using a vertical milling machine at a milling speed of 1500 RPM with a carbide end mill tool and a depth of cut of 2.5 mm, transforming the part into a milled part over a duration of 64 minutes, after which the milled part is placed on a conveyor belt.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel rotating at 3000 SFPM with a feed rate of 0.1 mm per revolution, resulting in a ground part, and the operation runs for 95 minutes before the output is transferred to a mobile robot.

The milled part is planed on a Planer for 94 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 3 mm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm per stroke, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On the Honing Machine, a honing operation is performed on the honed cylinder to achieve precise bore finishing, using a 220 grit honing stone to reach a final bore size of 50 mm, taking 46 minutes to complete, after which the precision finished part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal for 64 minutes, using a laser power of 3000 watts, a cutting speed of 2.5 m/min, and nitrogen as the gas assist, resulting in cut sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A milled part is shaped on a shaper using a high-speed steel tool with a stroke length of 300 mm and a shaping speed of 40 strokes per minute, lasting for 76 minutes, resulting in a shaped part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal fed from a conveyor belt, using a tungsten carbide blade with a 2-degree shear angle and a cutting speed of 1 cut per 10 seconds, processing the material for 77 minutes to produce sheared sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal, cutting it into sheared sheet metal using a high-carbon steel hardened blade at a shear angle of 2 degrees and a cutting speed of 15 strokes per minute, with the input material delivered by a MobileRobot and the output transferred to a ConveyorBelt, taking 75 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component loaded on a conveyor belt, using a laser power of 2500 W, a cutting speed of 3.5 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist at 20 bar, for 74 minutes, resulting in a cut sheet metal component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 32 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a speed of 180 strokes per minute, taking 82 minutes, after which the resulting shaped gear is placed on a conveyor belt.

The milled part is shaped using a shaper machine for 9 minutes, employing a high-speed steel single-point tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 40 rpm, resulting in a shaped part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling on the milled part for 75 minutes, using a 5-axis simultaneous tool configuration with a Ø12 mm end mill to achieve a milling precision of ±0.005 mm while engaging an active damping system for vibration control, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to the conveyor belt.

A lathed part is subjected to face and end milling on a vertical milling machine using a carbide face mill at a milling speed of 800 rpm and a depth of cut of 3 mm, processing for 87 minutes to produce a milled part that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component loaded by a mobile robot, using a Ø10 mm punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute with automatically calibrated die alignment, processing the material for 81 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

A planed part is loaded from a conveyor belt onto a grinding machine where it undergoes surface grinding using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/pass, transforming it into a ground part that is then transferred to a mobile robot, all taking 12 minutes.

On a Screw Machines, a lathed part is subjected to screw threading for 12 minutes, creating an M10 metric coarse thread at a production rate of 600 parts per hour, after which the resulting screwed component, still classified as a LathedPart, is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The milled part is planed on a Planer for 26 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2.5 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 mm/stroke, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 μm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

Using a horizontal milling machine, a slot milling operation is performed on the milled part loaded from the mobile robot, machining with linear interpolation at full depth and a milling speed of 600 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 μm, taking 18 minutes, and resulting in a finished machined component transferred to the conveyor belt.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on a honed cylinder, using a 220 grit honing stone to achieve a bore size of Ø50.000 ±0.005 mm, taking 89 minutes to complete, after which the precision finished part is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a shaped part is cut with brass-coated steel wire of Ø0.25 mm at a cutting speed of 8 mm/min and electrical parameters of 250 A peak current and 10 kHz frequency, performing Wire EDM Cutting for 84 minutes, after which the precision finished part is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a metal bar using a pull-type spline broach with a feed rate of 1.5 mm/stroke and a depth of cut of 4 mm, lasting for 87 minutes, resulting in a broached component that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to facing and turning operations for 14 minutes, using a ceramic insert (CCGT 672) tool at a spindle speed of 250 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Drill Press, a drilling operation is performed on a metal bar located on a conveyor belt, using a Ø12 mm drill at a spindle speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev, lasting for 93 minutes, resulting in a drilled component that is placed on a mobile robot.

The bandsaw performs a cutting to length operation on a metal bar, which is held by a mobile robot, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade at a saw speed of 60 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm, taking 20 minutes to complete, after which the resulting lathed part is placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component loaded from a conveyor belt, using a hobbing speed of 120 rpm and a feed rate of 0.8 mm/rev to produce an involute gear profile with a 20-degree pressure angle, lasting for 81 minutes, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The sheet metal is sheared on a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine using a high-speed steel blade with tungsten carbide edge at a shear angle of 2 degrees and a cutting speed of 30 meters per minute, processing for 93 minutes to produce sheared sheet metal, which is conveyed on the same conveyor belt.
Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 12 mm drill at a spindle speed of 850 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, resulting in a drilled component, and this operation takes 48 minutes.

A vertical turning operation is performed on a vertical lathe for 61 minutes, using a multi-pass facing and contouring toolpath with a precision level of ±0.02 mm, to shape a drilled component into a final drilled and shaped part, which remains in the mobile robot after processing.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, forming a spur gear with 24 teeth at a shaping speed of 60 strokes per minute, and the operation runs for 57 minutes, with the component loaded in and remaining in the MobileRobot throughout the process.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to rough turning for 89 minutes using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a spindle speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part.

On the CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed on the lathed part loaded in the MobileRobot, using G-code program #SHAFT-003 with a spindle speed of 750 rpm and tool offsets verified and calibrated for all 6 tools, resulting in a finished machined component, all for 62 minutes.

A milled part is machined using climb milling with a 75% stepover and a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm on a horizontal milling machine operating at a milling speed of 220 m/min, resulting in a finished machined component, all processed for 51 minutes.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on the honed cylinder, using a 180 mesh grit size to achieve a bore size of 50.00 ± 0.005 mm, resulting in a precision finished part, and the process runs for 89 minutes.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 m/min and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, resulting in a ground part, and the operation lasts for 43 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component located on the conveyor belt for 9 minutes, using a 3000-watt laser, a cutting speed of 4.5 meters per minute, and nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar, resulting in a cut sheet metal component that remains on the conveyor belt.

Using a Bandsaw, cold sawing is performed on a metal bar loaded on a MobileRobot for 73 minutes, operating at a saw speed of 60 m/min with a bi-metal variable pitch blade of 4 TPI and a cutting width of 3 mm kerf, resulting in a lathed part that remains on the MobileRobot.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a ground part is subjected to wire EDM cutting in fine finish mode with skim cuts and automatic edge stripping for deburring, using deionized water with conductivity less than 5 µS/cm as the dielectric fluid, resulting in a precision finished part, all processed for 24 minutes while both the input and output remain in the MobileRobot container.

On a Hobbing Machine, gear hobbing is performed on the broached component for 17 minutes, using a hobbing speed of 120 rpm and a feed rate of 1.2 mm/rev to produce an involute gear profile with a 20-degree pressure angle, resulting in a hobbied gear, both the input and output remaining in the MobileRobot.

On a Screw Machines, the Screw Threading operation is performed on a Lathed part loaded in a MobileRobot, creating metric coarse threads with 6g tolerance and M10 screw size at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, resulting in a Screwed component, and the process runs for 73 minutes.

Using a broaching machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part to create a spline, utilizing a pull-type spline broach with a precision level of ±0.015 mm, resulting in a broached component, and the process takes 12 minutes.

A milled part is subjected to multi-axis milling on a Stewart Platform Mills machine for 76 minutes, achieving a precision of ±0.008 mm using a 5-axis simultaneous tool configuration with a ball nose end mill and an active damping system engaged, resulting in a ground part delivered to the conveyor belt.

On the Punch Press, a punching operation is performed on sheet metal for 72 minutes, using a 25 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 120 strokes per minute and with die alignment automatically calibrated via optical sensor, transforming the input sheet metal on the conveyor belt into a finished sheet metal product that remains on the conveyor belt.

A milled part is shaped on a shaper using a high-speed steel single-point tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped part, and the operation takes 11 minutes.
The milled part is planed on a planer for 34 minutes, achieving a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm with a planing depth of 2.5 mm per pass and a feed rate of 0.4 mm/rev, resulting in a planed part.

On a Vertical Milling Machine, perform vertical milling with pocketing and contouring using a 3D toolpath on the cut sheet metal, achieving a tolerance of ±0.05 mm, resulting in a finished sheet metal product, and this operation takes 75 minutes.

On a Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched for 7 minutes using a 12 mm punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute with precision-aligned die for center punch, transforming it from a raw sheet metal on the conveyor belt into a finished sheet metal product in the form of a cut sheet metal, which remains on the conveyor belt after processing.

A metal bar is loaded on a mobile robot and undergoes roughing turning on a horizontal lathe using a carbide insert tool (TNMG 16 04 04) at a rotation speed of 450 RPM and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part, all for 62 minutes.

The sheet metal is sheared on a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine using a high-carbon steel, hardened blade at a shear angle of 1.5 degrees and a cutting speed of 10 m/min, transforming it into sheared sheet metal, and the operation takes 2 minutes.

On a Hobbing Machine, gear hobbing is performed on a broached component to produce a hobbied gear with an involute profile and 20-degree pressure angle, operating at a hobbing speed of 120 RPM and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev, and the operation runs for 28 minutes, with both the input and output components transported by a MobileRobot.

A lathed part is milled using a vertical milling machine through a vertical milling operation at a spindle speed of 1200 RPM with a 12 mm diameter, 4-flute end mill tool and a depth of cut of 3 mm, resulting in a milled part, and the process takes 73 minutes.
Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 10 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 900 RPM and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, resulting in a drilled component, and this operation takes 57 minutes.

A milled part is shaped on a shaper using a high-speed steel, single-point tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped part, and the operation runs for 51 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component placed on a conveyor belt, using a 3000-watt laser with nitrogen gas assist at 15 bar and a cutting speed of 5 m/min, transforming it into cut sheet metal over a duration of 75 minutes.

The bandsaw performs band sawing on a metal bar loaded from a mobile robot, cutting it into a lathed part using a bi-metal blade with 4/6 TPI and a cutting width of 0.5 mm at a saw speed of 60 m/min, and the operation takes 86 minutes to complete.

On the Honing Machine, the honed cylinder is precision honed using a 180 grit honing stone to achieve a bore size of 50 mm diameter, resulting in a precision finished part, with the operation lasting for 25 minutes and the component remaining in the MobileRobot before and after processing.

The milled part is planed on a planer for 98 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 mm/stroke, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part, with both the input and output handled by a mobile robot.

On a CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on a lathed part loaded in a MobileRobot, using CNC program #12-GS with verified and calibrated tool offsets and a spindle speed of 600 RPM, resulting in a finished machined component and taking 63 minutes.

On a Screw Machines, screw threading is performed on a lathed part to create an M12 metric coarse thread, processing at a rate of 120 parts per hour, and the operation takes 41 minutes, resulting in a screwed component that remains in the MobileRobot.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, forming a spur gear with 24 teeth at a shaping speed of 100 RPM, and the operation runs for 64 minutes, with the component loaded in and remaining in the MobileRobot throughout the process.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling on the milled part loaded in the MobileRobot, using a 5-axis synchronized tool configuration with an active damping system enabled to achieve a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, transforming it into a ground part over a duration of 24 minutes.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 62 minutes, using a ceramic insert tool (CCMT 12 04 08) at a rotation speed of 500 RPM and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that remains on the mobile robot.

On a Broaching Machine, a metal bar is broached using a pull-type broach with a feed rate of 1 mm/stroke and a depth of cut of 0.75 mm, producing a broached component, and this operation takes 40 minutes.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine for 21 minutes using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 RPM and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, resulting in a ground part, both transported by and from the machine via a mobile robot.

Using a horizontal milling machine, a milled part is machined via horizontal milling for 34 minutes at a milling speed of 1000 RPM using a climb milling tool path with a full slot strategy to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a finished machined component, both transported by and loaded on a mobile robot.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the shaped part loaded in the MobileRobot, using a brass wire with 0.25 mm diameter at a cutting speed of 8 mm/min and electrical parameters of 200 A peak current and 10 kHz frequency, producing a precision finished part in the same container over a duration of 44 minutes.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component placed on a conveyor belt, using a laser power of 2500 watts and a cutting speed of 15 meters per minute with nitrogen as the gas assist, transforming the input into cut sheet metal over a duration of 71 minutes.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 12 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm per revolution, resulting in a drilled component, and this operation takes 44 minutes.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 66 minutes using a carbide insert tool at a rotation speed of 600 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm per revolution, resulting in a lathed part.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component, using a 25 mm diameter punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute with automatic die centering, resulting in a finished cut sheet metal product, and this process runs for 93 minutes on the conveyor belt.

On a Broaching Machine, a metal bar is broached using a pull broach with a feed rate of 0.1 mm per stroke and a depth of cut of 3 mm, transforming it into a broached component, and this operation takes 61 minutes.

The bandsaw performs a sawing operation on a metal bar, using a bi-metal blade with a cutting width of 3 mm and a saw speed of 50 meters per minute, resulting in a lathed part, and this process takes 66 minutes, with the component loaded on a mobile robot before and after the operation.

On a Hobbing Machine, gear hobbing is performed on a broached component to produce a hobbied gear with an involute gear profile, operating at a hobbing speed of 120 rpm and a feed rate of 0.25 mm per revolution, and the process runs for 42 minutes, with both the input and output components transported by a MobileRobot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to horizontal turning for 51 minutes, using a high-speed steel tool at a rotation speed of 700 rpm and a feed rate of 0.18 mm per revolution, resulting in a lathed part.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling on a milled part loaded in a MobileRobot, using a 6-axis synchronized tool configuration with an active damping system to achieve a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, transforming it into a ground part, and this operation takes 32 minutes.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on the honed cylinder, using a honing grit size of 220 to achieve a bore size of 40 mm, resulting in a precision finished part, and this process runs for 52 minutes with both the input and output components transported by the mobile robot.

On a Screw Machines, a lathed part is processed for 31 minutes to perform Screw Threading with an M10 screw size and metric coarse thread type, producing a screwed component at a rate of 120 units per hour, with the component entering and exiting in a MobileRobot.

The shearing operation is performed on a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 30 minutes, where a sheet metal is cut using a hardened steel blade with a shear angle of 1.5 degrees and a cutting speed of 10 strokes per minute, resulting in sheared sheet metal, all conveyed via a conveyor belt.

The Shaper performs a shaping operation on the Milled part loaded in the MobileRobot, using a high-speed steel tool with a stroke length of 300 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute, transforming it into a Shaped part over a duration of 63 minutes.

The horizontal milling machine performs a horizontal milling operation on the milled part, using climb milling with a spindle speed of 1200 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 μm, transforming it into a finished machined component, and this process takes 29 minutes.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, processing for 90 minutes at a shaping speed of 60 rpm to form a 24-tooth spur gear, with the component loaded in and unloaded from the MobileRobot.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a shaped part is precision cut via wire EDM cutting for 75 minutes with a brass-coated steel wire, electrical parameters of 200 V and 10 A, and a cutting speed of 4 mm per minute, resulting in a precision finished part, both transported by a MobileRobot.

A CNC Turning operation is performed on a CNC Turning Center using G-code Program #7, with a spindle speed of 900 rpm and verified and calibrated tool offsets, processing the lathed part loaded on a MobileRobot for 94 minutes to produce a finished machined component, which remains on the MobileRobot.

A lathed part is milled using a vertical milling machine with a carbide end mill at a speed of 1500 rpm and a depth of cut of 2 mm, transforming it into a milled part, and the operation takes 9 minutes.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel rotating at 1800 rpm with a feed rate of 0.1 mm per pass, resulting in a ground part, and the operation lasts for 40 minutes.

The milled part is planed on a planer for 22 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 1.5 mm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm per stroke, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 μm, resulting in a planed part, with both the input and output handled by a mobile robot.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs shearing on a sheet metal component loaded from a conveyor belt, cutting it into a cut sheet metal piece using a high-speed steel straight edge blade at a shear angle of 2 degrees and a cutting speed of 15 meters per minute, taking 14 minutes to complete the operation, after which the sheared sheet metal is placed back on the conveyor belt.

The Laser Cutter performs laser cutting on a sheared sheet metal component, using a 3000-watt laser with a cutting speed of 10 meters per minute and nitrogen gas assist at 20 bar pressure, taking 46 minutes to complete, after which the resulting laser-cut sheet metal is placed on a conveyor belt.

A roughing milling operation is performed on a horizontal milling machine for 10 minutes, using a face milling tool path with 5mm stepover at a spindle speed of 800 RPM to achieve a surface finish of 6.3 micrometers Ra, starting with a pre-milled component of type MilledPart loaded from a conveyor belt and resulting in a rough-finished component of type MilledPart placed on a mobile robot.

On the Honing Machine, a honing operation is performed on a BoredCylinder to achieve a precise bore size of 50.00 mm ± 0.01 mm using a 150 grit honing stone, lasting for 52 minutes, resulting in a PrecisionBoreComponent that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The Planer performs surface planing on the MilledBlock, a milled part loaded on the conveyor belt, removing material at a depth of 1.2 mm per pass with a feed rate of 300 mm/min to achieve a surface finish of 3.2 micrometers Ra, taking 7 minutes to produce the FlatSurfacePart, which is then transferred to the mobile robot as a planed part.

On a Screw Machines, an Automatic Screw Threading operation is performed for 1 minute, threading a TurnedRod into a ThreadedComponent with M8 metric coarse threads at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, after which the finished ScrewedComponent is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

A metal bar stock is loaded from a conveyor belt onto a vertical lathe where it undergoes facing and turning operations for 13 minutes, using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a spindle speed of 450 RPM and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, resulting in a disc-shaped lathed part that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a PreDrilledBar (MetalBar) using an internal spline broach with a feed rate of 1 stroke per 2 minutes and a depth of cut of 3 mm total rise per tooth, lasting for 77 minutes, to produce a KeywayBroachedPart (BroachedComponent) that is then placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On a Vertical Milling Machine, precision pocket milling is performed on the LathedFlange, a lathed part retrieved from ConveyorBelt, using a 12mm diameter, 4-flute end mill at a milling speed of 1200 RPM and a depth of cut of 4 mm per pass, taking 37 minutes to produce the MilledFlangeWithPockets, which is then placed on a MobileRobot as a milled part.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed for 63 minutes to produce a 32-tooth spur gear by machining a BroachedGearBlank, which is delivered by a MobileRobot, using a shaping speed of 180 strokes per minute, resulting in a ShapedGear component named SpurGear that is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

Using the Stewart Platform Mills, the Ultra-Precision Milling operation processes the MilledHousing component, a MilledPart delivered on the ConveyorBelt, into the HighPrecisionHousing, a GroundPart, which is then transferred to the MobileRobot, for 37 minutes with a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, a 6-axis synchronized spindle tool configuration, and an active hydraulic damping system to minimize vibrations.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the ShapedDieComponent, using a 0.25mm brass wire and electrical parameters of 120V, 6A in micro-finish pulse mode at a cutting speed of 8 mm/min, resulting in the FinalPrecisionComponent, and the operation runs for 59 minutes, after which the ground part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

Using a bandsaw, cold sawing was performed on a long metal bar fed from a conveyor belt, cutting it into a lathed part with a bi-metal 4/6 TPI blade at a saw speed of 60 RPM and a cutting width of 3.2 mm kerf, taking 33 minutes to complete, after which the resulting cutoff bar for turning was transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a GearBlankWithBroach component to produce a FinishedHelicalGear with a helical gear profile and 20 degree pressure angle, running at a hobbing speed of 220 RPM and a feed rate of 1.5 mm/rev, lasting for 30 minutes, after which the hobbied gear is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Drill Press, a center drilling operation is performed on a SolidMetalBar to create a CenterDrilledBar, using a 10 mm drill at a spindle speed of 850 RPM and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, taking 78 minutes, with the input material loaded from a ConveyorBelt and the finished part transferred to a MobileRobot.

Perform finish turning on a CNC turning center using CNC Program #7A with verified and calibrated tool offsets and a spindle speed of 1100 RPM, processing the RoughTurnedPart for 38 minutes to produce the FullyFinishedShaft, which is then placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a rough turning operation is performed on a RawSteelBar taken from a ConveyorBelt, using a high-speed steel round nose tool at a rotation speed of 500 RPM and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, lasting for 77 minutes, resulting in a CylindricalShaftBlank that is placed on a MobileRobot.

Using a Punch Press, the FlatSheetBlank made of sheet metal is processed for 12 minutes to perform punching holes with a 12 mm round punch, a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute, and automatically calibrated die alignment, resulting in the finished PunchedPanel, which is then transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The PlanedGuideRail, a planed part on the conveyor belt, undergoes surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1500 m/min and a feed rate of 200 mm/min, resulting in the PrecisionGroundRail, a ground part, which is then placed on a mobile robot, all taking 46 minutes.

The Shaper performs a Keyway Shaping operation on the MilledKeyseatBlank, using a high-speed steel square nose tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute, processing the part for 33 minutes to produce the ShapedKeywayPart, which is then placed on the ConveyorBelt.

On a CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on a lathed part loaded from a MobileRobot, using CNC program #72-TC-FIN with calibrated tool offsets TO1-TO8 and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, resulting in a finished machined component loaded onto a ConveyorBelt, taking 72 minutes.

On the Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component to create an involute gear profile with a 20° pressure angle, running at a hobbing speed of 95 m/min and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev, lasting for 71 minutes, after which the hobbied gear is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 12.7 mm drill bit at a spindle speed of 850 rpm and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev, resulting in a drilled component, and the operation takes 84 minutes, after which the drilled component is placed on a conveyor belt.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling on the milled part for 10 minutes, using a 6-flute carbide end mill with a milling precision of ±0.005 mm and an active damping system engaged, transforming the input component into a ground part that is then placed on the conveyor belt.

The metal bar is loaded from the MobileRobot onto the Bandsaw, where it undergoes a sawing operation for 95 minutes using a bi-metal variable pitch blade at a saw speed of 60 m/min and a cutting width of 3.2 mm, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

A metal bar is loaded from a mobile robot onto a vertical lathe where it undergoes a rough turning operation for 24 minutes, using a carbide insert TNMG 16 04 04 tool at a rotation speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

The milled part is shaped using a shaper machine through a shaping operation lasting 18 minutes, employing a high-speed steel single-point tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 25 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the shaped part, using a 0.25 mm brass wire at electrical parameters of 12 A and 100 V with a cutting speed of 4 mm/min, resulting in a precision finished part, and the operation runs for 56 minutes, after which the milled part is placed on the conveyor belt.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to a facing and centering operation for 3 minutes using a carbide facing tool at a spindle speed of 600 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A planed part is loaded from a mobile robot onto a grinding machine where it undergoes surface grinding using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1750 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, transforming it into a ground part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt, with the entire operation lasting for 49 minutes.

On a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine, a sheet metal component is sheared into sheared sheet metal using a hardened steel, straight edge blade with a shear angle of 2° and a cutting speed of 10 cuts per minute, taking 77 minutes, with the input material delivered by a MobileRobot and the output placed on a ConveyorBelt.

Using a horizontal milling machine, a finish milling operation is performed on the milled part for 19 minutes at a milling speed of 2200 rpm, following a climb milling tool path with a full profile to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a metal bar using a pull-type spline broach with a feed rate of 0.03 mm/tooth and a depth of cut of 4.5 mm, resulting in a broached component, and the process takes 70 minutes, after which the broached component is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal, using a 3000 W laser with nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar and a cutting speed of 1.8 m/min, transforming the input material into cut sheet metal over a duration of 24 minutes, after which the finished part is transferred to the conveyor belt.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, processing it for 50 minutes with a shaping speed of 160 strokes/min to form a 32-tooth spur gear, after which the component is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On the Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched using a 25 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute with automatically calibrated die alignment, resulting in a finished cut sheet metal product, and the operation takes 19 minutes, after which the product is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On the Honing Machine, the honed cylinder is precision honed using a 150 mesh grit size to achieve a bore size of 45.0 ± 0.002 mm, resulting in a precision finished part, and the operation runs for 60 minutes before the ground part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The milled part is planed on a Planer for 45 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2.0 mm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/stroke to produce a planed part with a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, which is then transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Screw Machines, a lathed part is subjected to screw threading for 77 minutes, producing a screwed component with M10 metric coarse threads at a production rate of 120 pcs/hour, after which the output is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

A face milling operation is performed on a vertical milling machine for 6 minutes, using a lathed part as input, machining it with a square shoulder mill of 50 mm diameter at a milling speed of 1800 rpm and a depth of cut of 3.0 mm, resulting in a milled part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.
